The '''South African Mathematical Society (SAMS)''' is a professional mathematical society of [[South Africa]]. The Society was established in 1957.<ref>[http://www-history.mcs.st-and.ac.uk/Societies/South_African.html The South African Mathematical Society], [[MacTutor History of Mathematics archive]]. Accessed October 22, 2016</ref>
The SAMS publishes a research journal ''Quaestiones Mathematicae'', as well the ''Notices of the South African Mathematical Society'' (which serves as a general communications bulletin of the society), and holds its Annual Congress. The Society also helps represent South African mathematics and mathematicians in various national and international structures, including the [[International Mathematical Union]], [[African Mathematical Union]], [[Southern Africa Mathematical Sciences Association]], Association for [[Mathematics education|Mathematics Education]] of South Africa, and others.

The SAMS has more than 300 members.

==History==

The South African Mathematical Society was established in 1957, originally under the English name  'The South African Mathematical Association' and the corresponding [[Afrikaans]] name ‘Die Suid-Afrikaanse Wiskundige Vereniging’.<ref name=Maritz>P. Maritz, [http://www.sams.ac.za/history.html The South African Mathematical Society 1957 - 2007],  South African Mathematical Society. Accessed October 22, 2016.</ref> Dr Johann van der Mark from the Mathematics Division, National Physics Research Laboratory, [[Institute of Physics]] of the Council for Scientific and Industrial Research (CSIR) in Pretoria, was a key figure in setting up and launching the South African Mathematical Association.<ref name=Maritz/>  The first Chairman of the Council of the Association, for the period 1957–1958, was James M. Hyslop ([[University of the Witwatersrand]]).<ref name=Maritz/>

The SAMS was one of the groups involved in launching, in 1992–1993 the new ''Association for Mathematics Education of South Africa'' (AMESA),<ref>[http://www.amesa.org.za/History.htm History of AMESA], Association for Mathematics Education of South Africa. Accessed October 23, 2016</ref> a professional association for mathematics [[education in South Africa]].

===SAMS and apartheid===

From the moment the SAMS was launched in 1957, its Constitution, membership, election and office-holder rules were non-discriminatory and did not contain any racially restrictive language. In August 1962 the SAMS Council decided that, notwithstanding the apartheid laws and social expectations in the country, the SAMS would not form separate branches of the SAMS for non-white members.<ref name=M>P. Maritz, [http://www.sams.ac.za/history-increasemath.html The South African Mathematical Society 1957 – 2007Section H: Delicate Issues.] South African Mathematical Society. Accessed October 23, 2016</ref> 
Nevertheless, until the early 1990s, the SAMS had only a few non-white members; thus the Society had two black members in 1977 and four in 1980.<ref name=M/>

During the [[apartheid]] era, the SAMS continued to experience difficulties it terms of its international recognition and international activities because of the general international human rights, protest and boycott movements directed against the South African regime.  Thus the [[American Mathematical Society]] originally established a reciprocity agreement with the SAMS in 1972, after an investigation by the AMS showed that the membership rules for admittance to the SAMS were non-discriminatory. However, after protests by civil rights activists, the AMS cancelled the reciprocity agreement in 1974.<ref>Everett Pitcher, [https://books.google.com/books?id=JY3OxdP0h5cC&dq=%22south+african+mathematical+society%22&pg=PA156 A history of the second fifty years, American Mathematical Society 1939–88], [[American Mathematical Society]], 1988,  {{isbn|978-0-8218-0125-3}}; p. 156</ref><ref>Charlene Morrow, Teri Perl, [https://books.google.com/books?id=u7nqH3RzUusC&dq=%22south+african+mathematical+society%22&pg=PA73 Notable Women in Mathematics: A Biographical Dictionary], Greenwood Press, 1998, {{isbn|0313291314}}; p. 73</ref> The AMS restored its reciprocity agreement with the SAMS in 1994, after the fall of the apartheid.<ref>[[Bettye Anne Case]], [https://books.google.com/books?id=UnkYqxyWGz8C&dq=%22south+african+mathematical+society%22&pg=PA101 A Century of Mathematical Meetings], [[American Mathematical Society]], 1995, {{isbn|0821804650}}; p 90</ref>
The SAMS annual Distinguished Visitor program experienced a high rate of declined invitations and postponed visits due to concerns of the international mathematical community about the apartheid.<ref name=M/> One of the most publicized visits under the program was that of [[Peter Hilton]], who was the SAMS Distinguished Visitor for 1981. Hilton published a letter in the [[Notices of the American Mathematical Society]], prior to his visit, explaining the conditions on which he accepted the visit<ref name=M/> and later published an account of his visit.<ref>[[Peter Hilton]], [http://www.maa.org/sites/default/files/pdf/pubs/focus/past_issues/FOCUS_1_4.pdf Reflections on a visit to South Africa], ''Focus'', vol. 1, no. 4, Nov. – Dec 1981. [[Mathematical Association of America]]</ref>

==Membership==

Generally, membership in SAMS requires holding a [[Bachelor of Science|bachelor's degree]], or its equivalent, in a mathematical discipline. Admission to membership requires nomination by two current members of the Society and must be approved by the SAMS Council.<ref name=Const/>

At present there are four membership categories:<ref name=Const>[http://www.sams.ac.za/constitution Constitution.] South African Mathematical Society. Accessed October 23, 2016</ref>

*Full members
*Special members, eligible for reduced membership fees (often applicable to graduate students and retirees, and to members of foreign mathematical societies with which the SAMS has reciprocity agreements)
*Institutional members (applies to certain institutions that are regarded as a single member of the SAMS)
*Honorary members

==Awards==

The SAMS grants two awards:

* '''The SAMS Award for Research Distinction''', awarded for outstanding research achievements, to "recognise and reward substantial research carried out in South Africa, which does credit to South African Mathematics".<ref name=awards>[http://www.sams.ac.za/awards-of-sams Awards of the SAMS], South African Mathematical Society. Accessed March 7, 2022.</ref>
* '''The SAMS Award for the Advancement of Mathematics''', "to recognise and reward exceptional and distinguished service to the cultivation of Mathematics in South Africa".<ref name=awards/>

The SAMS also has one student award:

*   The '''SAMS Bronze Medal''' is awarded to the best honors students in Mathematics or [[Applied mathematics|Applied Mathematics]] at South African universities.<ref>[http://www.sams.ac.za/sams-bronze-medal SAMS Bronze Medal], South African Mathematical Society. Accessed March 7, 2021.</ref>
